audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t states 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.' That is the wrong conclusion: Grievous Wounds reduces healing by source-agnostic percentage, so it cuts Soul Ignition's refund exactly like any other heal. Nothing on the page mentions that Silver Stake's on-hit scales with MISSING health, or that Ashen Pursuit is an auto reset.
audit.why: Riot's W text: 'At the end of the duration, Locke will heal back a portion of the damage he takes during the effect.' That is healing, and it is the biggest single number in an extended trade against him. Riot's passive: 'additional magic damage On-Hit, increased based on enemy missing Health' — so the trade gets worse the longer you stay low, which inverts the usual 'stay and finish it' instinct.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now calls for Grievous Wounds against the Soul Ignition refund; dontsFull[0].d states the missing-health scaling; dosFull[2].d names Ashen Pursuit's auto reset as the wind-up tell.

notes: Two things I would not assert without a ruling, both recorded rather than edited. (1) NAME: the page calls Locke's Q 'Ritual Nails' everywhere (focus.text, winCon, enemyWin, the cooldown block, report[5]). Riot's own Q text in the kit says 'Locke readies a set of SOUL Nails to throw'. The kit file carries no ability names for Locke at all (packet.enemyAbilities is null), and the only names available anywhere in the brief come from the missing-interactions headlines: Silver Stake (P), Soul Ignition (W), Ashen Pursuit (E). So 'Ritual Nails' and 'Purgatory' are unverifiable from the data I have, and 'Ritual Nails' actively conflicts with the one piece of Riot text that mentions nails. I did not rename anything — this is a champion-wide string that appears in a dozen fields and getting it wrong in either direction is worse than leaving it. (2) The supplied missing-interaction 'Locke bypasses stacking resistances (Soul Ignition (W))' looks like a tooltip-parsing misfire in the same family the instructions warn about: the trueDamage flag sits on an ability whose only damage in Riot's text is damage Locke deals TO HIMSELF. I wrote no 'armour is the wrong answer' advice on the strength of it.
